questions.explanation: A limit describes the value that f(x) approaches as x approaches a, not necessarily the value at x = a. The function may even be undefined at a and still have a limit.
options: f(x) gets arbitrarily close to L as x gets close to a, and f(a) need not equal L
f(x) grows without bound as x approaches a
x equals L whenever f(x) equals a
questions.question: Which statement best describes what lim x→a f(x) = L means?

questions.correct_answer: The instantaneous rate of change of f at x = a, equal to the slope of the tangent line there
questions.explanation: The derivative at a point is the limit of average rates of change over shrinking intervals, which gives the instantaneous rate of change and the slope of the tangent line at that point.
options: The average value of f on the interval from 0 to a
The total area under the graph of f from 0 to a
The instantaneous rate of change of f at x = a, equal to the slope of the tangent line there
The value f(a) of the function at x = a
questions.question: What does the derivative f'(a) represent?

questions.correct_answer: The limit of f(x) as x approaches a exists and equals f(a)
questions.explanation: Continuity at a point requires three things: f(a) is defined, the limit as x approaches a exists, and the two values are equal. Failing any one of these makes f discontinuous at a.
options: f has a derivative equal to zero at x = a
f(a) is defined and f is increasing near a
The limit of f(x) as x approaches a exists, even if f(a) is undefined
The limit of f(x) as x approaches a exists and equals f(a)
